headline: CISA gave federal agencies until Friday to patch a maximum-severity ColdFusion flaw and three other actively exploited bugs, as researchers exposed fresh data-leaking holes in Google's and GitHub's AI agent platforms.

emerging_trends.text: Fresh flaws in Google's Dialogflow CX chatbots and GitHub's agentic workflows show that the platforms enterprises trust to run autonomous AI agents now form a poorly guarded attack surface.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Agent Platforms Leak Private Data

emerging_trends.text: Two decades-old Linux kernel bugs surfaced this week, and GhostLock alone hands any logged-in user full root on nearly every mainstream distribution shipped since 2011.
emerging_trends.topic_title: GhostLock Kernel Flaw and Ubiquiti UniFi Bugs

emerging_trends.text: CISA gave federal agencies until Friday to close the maximum-severity ColdFusion path-traversal bug attackers already exploit, one of four flaws it rushed into its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
emerging_trends.topic_title: CISA Rushes ColdFusion, Langflow, and Joomla Patches

topics.title: CISA Rushes ColdFusion, Langflow, and Joomla Patches
topics.latest_developments: CISA added four actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on July 7—Adobe ColdFusion path-traversal bug CVE-2026-48282 rated 10.0, Langflow authorization-bypass CVE-2026-55255, and the Joomla page-builder flaws CVE-2026-48908 and CVE-2026-56290—and ordered agencies to patch by Friday, July 10, as researchers confirmed attackers exploiting Gitea flaw CVE-2026-20896.
topics.summary: ColdFusion runs web applications, Langflow builds AI agents, and the JoomShaper and Joomlack page builders power Joomla sites; attackers use all four for code execution or authentication bypass, and CISA requires every federal agency to apply the vendor fixes.

sources.title: CISA Adds 4 Actively Exploited Adobe, Joomla, and Langflow Flaws to KEV
CISA orders feds to patch max severity ColdFusion flaw by Friday
CISA orders feds to prioritize patching Langflow auth bypass flaw
Critical Gitea Flaw Under Active Exploitation, Researchers Warn

topics.title: AI Agent Platforms Leak Private Data
topics.latest_developments: Varonis disclosed a now-patched rogue-agent flaw in Google's Dialogflow CX that let anyone with edit rights on one Code Block agent hijack other agents in the same Google Cloud project to read live conversations and steal data, Noma Security showed a public GitHub issue can trick GitHub Agentic Workflows into leaking an organization's private repositories through a bug dubbed GitLost, and ESET counted more than 25,000 suspicious skills among nearly 900,000 it analyzed.
topics.summary: Enterprises wiring autonomous AI agents into Google Cloud, GitHub, and third-party skill marketplaces open new paths for data theft; defenders should audit agent permissions, restrict cross-repository read access, and vet installed skills.

sources.title: Dialogflow CX 'Rogue Agent' Flaw Enabled AI Chatbot Data Theft
'GitLost' Flaw Leaks Private Data From GitHub's Agentic Workflows
Public GitHub Issue Could Trick GitHub Agentic Workflows Into Leaking Private Repo Data
Thousands of malicious AI skills found capable of stealing data, running malware

topics.title: GhostLock Kernel Flaw and Ubiquiti UniFi Bugs
topics.latest_developments: Nebula Security disclosed GhostLock, CVE-2026-43499, a 15-year-old Linux kernel flaw that gives any logged-in user full root and container escape on essentially every mainstream distribution shipped since 2011, the same day Ubiquiti patched seven critical UniFi OS bugs including a maximum-severity command-injection flaw.
topics.summary: GhostLock needs no special permissions, unusual settings, or network access and affects default kernels dating to 2011; administrators should apply the kernel and UniFi OS updates without delay.

sources.title: 15-Year-Old GhostLock Flaw Enables Root and Container Escape on Most Linux Distros
Ubiquiti warns of new max severity UniFi OS vulnerability

topics.title: China's UAT-7810 Grows LONGLEASH ORB Network
topics.latest_developments: Cisco Talos attributed new bespoke malware called LONGLEASH to the Chinese advanced persistent threat UAT-7810, which breaks into internet-facing networking gear, chiefly unpatched Ruckus routers, to expand LapDogs, the Operational Relay Box proxy network Talos first exposed in June 2025.
topics.summary: Operational Relay Box networks route espionage traffic through hijacked edge devices to hide the attacker's origin; UAT-7810 targets exposed Ruckus routers, so operators should patch or replace vulnerable networking hardware.

sources.title: China-Linked UAT-7810 Expands ORB Network With New LONGLEASH Malware
Chinese hackers develop LONGLEASH malware to expand ORB network

topics.title: Google Sues Gemini-Powered Phishing Service
topics.latest_developments: Google sued Outsider Enterprise, a China-based crew that sells phishing-as-a-service over Telegram and coaches customers to use Google's Gemini AI to spin up fake Google, YouTube, and other login pages, as Dark Reading detailed a parallel campaign impersonating big brands in fake job offers to steal marketing professionals' Google credentials.
topics.summary: Criminals now lean on Gemini to mass-produce convincing phishing sites for non-technical buyers; the lawsuit and the jobs-scam research both center on credential theft aimed at Google accounts.

sources.title: Google Is Suing Chinese Scammers Who Are Using Gemini
Big Brand Jobs Scam Targets Marketing Pros' Google Accounts

topics.title: RedWing Rents Android Bank Fraud
topics.latest_developments: Zimperium's zLabs uncovered RedWing, a new Android bank-fraud service rented over Telegram that hands low-skill criminals full takeover of a victim's phone to steal banking logins and intercept the one-time codes protecting accounts, and identified it as a fresh variant of the $300-a-month Oblivion rent-a-malware tool.
topics.summary: RedWing lowers the barrier to mobile bank fraud by packaging device takeover, credential theft, and one-time-code capture as a rental; Android users should avoid sideloaded apps and unexpected accessibility-permission requests.

sources.title: RedWing MaaS Packages Android Bank Fraud as a Telegram Rental Service

business_politics.title: Trump Declares Iran Ceasefire Over as Oil Jumps
business_politics.latest_developments: President Trump publicly said the June ceasefire with Iran is "over" after a fresh round of tit-for-tat strikes, driving Brent crude up 6% and pushing 10-year U.S., German, and U.K. bond yields to four-week highs.
business_politics.summary: The United States and Iran traded fresh strikes after attackers hit three merchant ships off Oman, and Trump said the interim peace deal he signed in mid-June has collapsed; oil jumped roughly 6%, the dollar turned higher, gold held above $4,100 an ounce, European gas prices climbed, and global stocks slumped.

business_politics.latest_developments: UniCredit said it lifted its voting rights in Commerzbank to 48% after the tender period closed, moving to the brink of majority control of the German lender.
business_politics.summary: Italy's UniCredit has raised its stake in Frankfurt-based Commerzbank to 48%, closing in on the first majority takeover of a large German bank by a foreign rival, a cross-border consolidation Berlin has resisted.

business.title: Garrity Calls for Pause on Data Centers
business.latest_developments: At a Butler County listening session, Republican gubernatorial nominee Stacy Garrity explicitly called for a pause on Pennsylvania data-center development, hardening a stance she had earlier treaded carefully around.
business.summary: Stacy Garrity, the Republican nominee for Pennsylvania governor, told a Butler County audience she wants a moratorium on new data centers over concerns about local input and protections for electricity ratepayers, and she accused Governor Josh Shapiro of lacking a firm position on the projects.
